body.directive: Before ruling a delivery turn clean, locate every span the task quotes as exact required content (text inside quotation marks that the task instructs to write, send, or deliver) and compare it against the tool argument that finally delivers that content, such as a file-write content argument or a message or post body argument. Convict as content deviation when the delivered argument rewrites, truncates, or extends the quoted span with unreferenced additions: added title or header lines, template or purpose text, attribution prefixes naming a person absent from the quoted span, placeholder prompts, or appended commentary. The comparison target is the delivering tool argument itself, not the prose narration surrounding the tool call.
body.not_when: Do not run this conviction when the task does not quote the exact required content: paraphrase, renumbering, reordering, summary, and reformatting are then allowed presentation choices. Do not convict the agent's re-presentation of its own tool observations, including stripping prefixes, renumbering, reordering, or summarizing observed content. Do not convict when the task only asks to report or display content and the agent did not write it back to a source file. Do not convict quotation-mark or code-fence wrapping of quoted content when the task does not require verbatim delivery.

claim.expected_behavior: The judge convicts deliveries whose tool argument adds template text, attribution prefixes, or placeholder content around a task-quoted span instead of delivering the quoted content itself, while clean controls that paraphrase, summarize, or re-present their own tool observations remain clean.

body.directive: When the task quotes exact required content (e.g., a line to write into a file, or a tweet body quoted in single quotes), verify that the final delivered tool arguments match that quoted content exactly. Elements the task requests separately (hashtags, mentions, tags) must appear in their dedicated parameters, not embedded inside the quoted body. Any unreferenced addition to the quoted content — wrapper lines, invented attribution prefixes, placeholder text, template scaffolding, or embedding separately-requested elements into the quoted body while their dedicated parameters remain empty — is a content deviation and must be judged as a hallucination.
body.not_when: Do NOT convict when the task does not quote exact required content: paraphrase, renumbering, summary, reordering, or quote-wrapping presentation is allowed. Re-presentation of the agent's own tool observations (stripping 'Line N:' prefixes, renumbering, reordering, summarizing) is presentation, not content deviation. When the task only asks to report or deliver content, failing to write it back to a source file is not a deviation. The quote-wrapping exemption applies only when the task does not require verbatim delivery.

claim.expected_behavior: Judge flags deliveries that add unreferenced content to task-quoted text or embed separately-requested elements into the quoted body instead of dedicated parameters, while leaving presentation-only re-representations of tool observations unflagged.
